visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The video opens with a top-down shot of three pen boxes placed on a brown, textured carpet: a large white Visconti box, a small tan TWSBI box, and a medium black Aurora box. A hand enters the frame and taps the black box. (2) The hand opens the Visconti box, which features a colorful reproduction of Van Gogh's 'The Novel Reader' on its lid. Inside, a dark green fountain pen with gold accents is revealed against a grey lining. (3) Focus shifts to the Aurora black box. The hand scratches the textured red letters spelling 'VELVET', showing the fuzzy material. (4) The hand opens the Aurora box to show a bright hot-pink fountain pen with a matching velvet texture and silver hardware. The hand picks up and rotates the pen to show the material's sheen. (5) The tan TWSBI box is opened, revealing a clear-bodied fountain pen with mint-green marbled plastic on the cap and piston knob. (6) A close-up shows the pink velvet pen writing Chinese characters on grid paper. The ink is a deep blue and appears quite wet. (7) The final shot shows a page filled with neat blue ink calligraphy on grid paper as the camera pans down.

audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) A clear, female voice begins narrating over a relaxing acoustic guitar and piano BGM track. The music is cheerful and steady. (2) A sharp, short mechanical slide and paper-like rustle are heard as the first pen box is opened. (3) A continuous, high-frequency rhythmic scratching sound occurs as the narrator rubs her fingers over the velvet box texture. (4) The narrator's pitch increases and she says 'Wow' in response to the pink pen, indicating pleasant surprise. (5) Another set of plastic sliding sounds and a soft click are heard while opening the transparent pen case. (6) The sound of the pen nib meeting paper creates a series of dry, scratchy transients as the character writes.

narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video serves as a specialized stationery unboxing and review. It aims to showcase the unique aesthetic and tactile qualities of three distinct fountain pens (Visconti, Aurora, TWSBI) to hobbyists, focusing on the sensory experience of the velvet texture and the writing quality of the nibs.
